## Design note

The everyday missile. All its weight sits over the rear wheels, so it launches like nothing else in the city and the short wheelbase lets it dart through traffic, but lift off mid-corner and the tail swings like a pendulum. The front coupling sends a third of the drive forward, enough to launch it cleanly but not enough to stop the tail stepping out. Built to be driven every day: the toughest of the supercars.

## How this car breaks

Steel-and-aluminium unibody with a proper engine lid, not a tub — more crumple length up front (the luggage bay) than the mid-engine cars, so nose hits are cheap. The engine and gearbox hang behind the rear axle on the rear subframe, right where a rear-ender lands: one firm rear hit stops it dead. The rear-engine layout is approximated with the mid-engine lattice (engine just behind the cabin). Durability class 4: at strength 1.0 the short-wheelbase nose crushed 1.61 m at 56 km/h (band 0.35-1.3); a daily-driver unibody with a front luggage bay is a proper modern crash structure.

## Inertia

Box approximation about the CG, scaled for mass concentration (`k < 1`: mass near the centre, e.g. mid-engine; `k → 1`: mass at the ends):

```
I_roll  = k_r · m·(W² + H²)/12
I_pitch = k_p · m·(L² + H²)/12
I_yaw   = k_y · m·(W² + L²)/12
```

| Axis | Box (kg·m²) | k | `inertia_kgm2` |
|---|---|---|---|
| roll | 746 | 0.82 | 610 |
| pitch | 3141 | 0.90 | 2830 |
| yaw | 3411 | 0.88 | 3000 |

## Aerodynamics

Frontal area A = 0.84·W·H = 2.07 m²; Cd = 0.33 → **CdA = 0.685 m²**. Lift Cl·A front/rear = -0.04 / -0.10 m² (class-typical; positive = lift). Add-on aero `aero_downforce_coeffs` = 0.04 F / 0.10 R m² (adaptive front lip and extending rear spoiler at its performance setting). Net downforce Cl·A 0.08 F / 0.20 R m² → 84 kg at 250 km/h, 29% front (static weight 39% front).

## Engine

3.8 L DOHC 24-valve horizontally opposed six, twin variable-geometry turbos, intercooled. Class-typical 2020s 3.8 TT flat-six (~124 kW/L, ~470 kW at 6500-7000 rpm, 800 N·m from 2500) per manufacturer spec-class data and owner dyno sheets; variable-geometry turbos give the earliest full torque of the supercars.

## Drivetrain

8-speed dual-clutch, rear-biased AWD (multi-plate front coupling modelled as a fixed 30 % front split: `AwdOnDemand` is built for front-biased cars and never closed at launch, 4.85 s 0-100 measured), clutch-type rear LSD. Layout **AWD, 30 % front**; front diff: open; rear diff: clutch LSD, preload 60 N·m, power ramp 0.45, coast ramp 0.30. Clutch capacity 1.40 × peak torque = 1120 N·m. Shift time 0.18 s.

## Suspension

Springs from ride frequency, `k = m_s·(2πf)²` with sprung corner mass `m_s = axle load/2 − unsprung`; dampers `c = 2ζ·√(k·m_s)`, ζ = 0.32 bump, rebound = 1.5 × bump.

| Axle | m_s | f | Wheel rate k | Bump c | Rebound c | Travel |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Front | 308 kg | 2.05 Hz | 51000 N/m | 2540 N·s/m | 3810 N·s/m | 0.12 m |
| Rear | 489 kg | 2.15 Hz | 89300 N/m | 4230 N·s/m | 6340 N·s/m | 0.13 m |

Anti-roll bars from a roll-gradient target of 1.5°/g with 56% of roll stiffness at the front. Roll arm h − h_rc = 0.346 m (roll centres 0.08 m F / 0.12 m R). Required total K_φ = m·g·arm/φ = 218863 N·m/rad; springs give k·t²/2 = 64500 F / 108687 R N·m/rad; bars supply the rest as `arb_n_per_m = K_bar/t²` = **23000 F / 0 R N/m** (clamped at ≥ 0). Resulting gradient 1.4°/g, front share 53%. Bump stops 200000 N/m.

Alignment: camber -1.5° F / -1.8° R, toe +0.00° F / +0.25° R (+ = in), caster 8.0°.

## Brakes

Full-pedal line pressure 100 bar.

- Front: 420 mm disc, pistons per side 40 mm + 36 mm + 32 mm → A = 30.8 cm², r_eff = D/2 − 25 mm = 185 mm, pad μ = 0.46: T = 2·μ·p·A·r_eff = 2·0.46·100 bar·30.8 cm²·0.185 m = **5240 N·m**
- Rear: 410 mm disc, pistons per side 40 mm + 36 mm → A = 22.7 cm², r_eff = D/2 − 25 mm = 180 mm, pad μ = 0.45: T = 2·μ·p·A·r_eff = 2·0.45·100 bar·22.7 cm²·0.180 m = **3685 N·m**

ABS ceiling: caliper capacity 5240 / 3685 N·m exceeds 1.5 × the front lock torque on this car's tire (peak μ 1.20), which `wp_vehicle`'s ABS cannot modulate (it releases to a fraction of the commanded torque, so an oversized caliper keeps the wheel locked). Both axles scaled by 0.54 → **2850 / 2000 N·m**. Remove when 02's ABS modulates relative to lock torque.

Lock check at 1 g on μ = 1 (load transfer m·a·h/L): front needs 1583 N·m/wheel (capacity 1.80×), rear needs 1238 N·m/wheel (capacity 1.62×).

`wp_vehicle` gives the axle `bias_front` favours its full `max_torque_*` and scales the other by (1 − b)/b, so `max_torque_*` holds the caliper capacity per wheel and `bias_front` acts as the proportioning valve: the rear is trimmed to the same lock margin as the front (ideal rear = T_f · lock_r/lock_f = 2229 N·m), never boosted above its caliper capacity. Rear capacity is below that (hardware-limited rear), so `bias_front` = **0.5**: both axles get full caliper torque → delivered 2850 N·m front / 2000 N·m rear per wheel at full pedal. Handbrake 2650 N·m per rear wheel.

## Steering

Ratio 13.0:1. Kerb-to-kerb turning circle 10.8 m → outer-front path radius 5.27 m, rear-axle-centre radius 3.87 m → mean road-wheel lock δ = atan(L/R) = **0.564 rad (32.3°)** (outer 27.7°, inner 38.5° at full Ackermann; `ackermann_frac` 0.60). Rack speed 1.8 rad/s.

## Damage lattice (`data/lattices/ostwind_6t.json`)

289 nodes, 1853 beams, 6 detachables, 21 component mounts.

- Generated with `gen-lattice --id ostwind_6t --profile coupe --width 1.9 --length 4.54 --height 1.3 --wheelbase 2.45 --mass 354.9 --car-mass 1690.0 --clearance 0.12 --front-overhang 0.97 --strength 1.15` (21% of vehicle mass in the lattice; strength from durability class 4).
- Era `2020s`: gen-lattice's default HSS passenger cell kept as is.
- Aluminium body: 663 outer-panel beams mild_steel → aluminum.
- Mid-engine: engine block moved behind the cabin bulkhead (y -0.99…-1.64 m), mounted to the rear rails and the bulkhead; 10 nodes behind the bulkhead relabelled FrameRear (engine bay, not cabin); 16 front-rail beams × 1.6 (no engine block in the nose: they get gen-lattice's rear-rail factor); 194 rear-subframe beams → aluminum ×1.5 section (sacrificial); gearbox and half-shafts at the rear axle, side fuel tanks at the sills behind the seats; engine fails at 0.12 m, gearbox 0.08 m.
- Front luggage bay framed by steel crash rails (rear-engine car: the nose is a full crumple zone): 16 front-rail beams × 1.80 section.
